title: ChatGPT Client Acquisition System
audience: Independent developers whose prospecting process already works but keeps disappearing from the calendar as soon as paid client work gets busy.
shortDescription: Keep research, pipeline review, follow-up checks, and reporting moving on schedule without jumping straight to APIs or giving up the human review that protects quality.
coreOutcome: Turn a proven manual campaign into a scheduled routine that keeps showing up even during busy delivery weeks, while Google Sheets preserves what happened and what needs attention next.
problem: The campaign works when you remember to run it, but the exact weeks when you are busiest are also the weeks that quietly create next month's empty pipeline.
hook: Your prospecting system should not stop because client work got busy.
reframe:
The dangerous thing about a good client month is how easy it is to stop doing the work that creates the next one. Delivery expands, follow-up gets pushed to Friday, Friday disappears, and a few weeks later you are finishing a project with less pipeline than you thought.

If the underlying campaign is still uncertain, scheduling it only makes uncertainty recur on time. But once you already know how to define the buyer, verify evidence, qualify a lead, write from approved facts, and stop when someone replies or opts out, repeating the same reviews manually becomes memory work.

The ChatGPT Client Acquisition System moves recurring research, pipeline review, follow-up checks, and reporting onto a schedule while Google Sheets keeps durable state. Scheduled does not mean reckless. Human checkpoints remain where evidence or judgment matters. The payoff is simple: prospecting is less likely to vanish just because the work you won is now consuming your attention.

delivery.length: Implementation guide for scheduled, no-API prospecting with ChatGPT and Google Workspace.
delivery.worksheets: Campaign state model, scheduled task definitions, review checkpoints, suppression rules, follow-up states, and reporting setup.
delivery.time: Implement after Tier 1 rules are stable enough that you are repeating the same decisions consistently.

proof.title: The next run remembers what the last one already did.
proof.body: A schedule is only useful when it continues a campaign instead of rediscovering it. Google Sheets stores campaign, lead, activity, follow-up, and suppression state so recurring work can surface what needs attention next without duplicating yesterday.
proof.before: Remember to research new leads, check who needs follow-up, search Gmail for replies, and update the tracker whenever client work leaves enough time.
proof.after: Run scheduled jobs against durable state, surface the items that need review, update the record, and keep human approval before sensitive actions.

situation: A validated campaign still depends on you remembering every recurring research, review, follow-up, and reporting task.
commonFailure: Adding schedules without durable state, suppression, and review checkpoints creates duplicate work and makes an inconsistent campaign recur more reliably.
methodology: Store campaign state in Google Sheets, schedule recurring ChatGPT work, review evidence and outreach decisions, update state after each action, and keep suppression and reporting explicit.
capabilities: Keep recurring prospecting work visible during busy client weeks
Maintain enough state that scheduled runs know what already happened

faqs.question: Do I need API access?
faqs.answer: No. This tier is intentionally built around ChatGPT, Google Drive, Google Sheets, Gmail, and recurring tasks so you can remove memory work before taking on API infrastructure.

faqs.question: Is this fully autonomous?
faqs.answer: No. The point is reliable recurrence, not removing judgment. Human review remains part of the operating model where evidence quality or sensitive actions matter.

faqs.question: Why use Google Sheets as state?
faqs.answer: At this level, Sheets gives you visible durable state without forcing a small campaign to become a software project before it needs to.

faqs.question: When should I move to Tier 3?
faqs.answer: Move up when the frustrating part is no longer remembering the work. Move when tool-to-tool handoffs themselves are consuming enough attention to justify n8n, APIs, retries, deduplication, and exception handling.

stateModel: Google Sheets as durable campaign state
supervision: Scheduled execution with regular human review
technicalBoundary: This tier does not center on n8n orchestration, custom API pipelines, application databases, or worker infrastructure.
